conclusion: A CPU-less runtime SimObject graph and a CPU-less link configuration are separate claims from the host ELF symbol closure; generic BaseCPU/System symbols in a monolithic x86-64 binary do not prove runtime CPU instantiation.
decision: Report runtime object counts and binary/link identities independently, and state the CP20 boundary as no runtime CPU/Process/Ruby/TLB/HSAPP/GPUCommandProcessor objects rather than as a universal CPU-free ELF claim.
invalidated_assumptions: A generic BaseCPU or System symbol in the monolithic ELF means a CPU or System object was instantiated in the B2 runtime graph.
A zero CPU-object count alone proves that every host-side binary dependency is non-x86.
observation: The CP20 runtime graph contains 79 objects and zero CPU, Process, Ruby, TLB, HSAPP, GPUCommandProcessor, and AMDGPUDevice objects, while the retained x86-64 executable still contains generic BaseCPU/System symbols.
question_or_symptom: How should a no-x86 execution result describe runtime ownership without overclaiming from linker symbols?
